title: Qwen3.8 Flash Next API Pricing: Token Costs (2026)
summary: Qwen3.8 Flash Next API pricing varies by tier with different rate limits and token costs. Compare plans to calculate your expected monthly expenses.
body_markdown:
## Model Routing and Spend Checks in Activepieces


The larger model only runs where a step has earned it, and in Activepieces that routing sits on your own provider key, so the model spend lands on your provider account at your own rate; MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


The provider's own limits catch whatever the workflow misses.


### Spending Rules for Qwen3.8 Flash Next Automation Steps


Every automated step now answers to five rules. Classification and triage go to the cheapest model that gets them right. Drafting, where tone and length matter, goes to a larger one.


The workflow caps retries at two, so a failing step stops instead of re-billing the same prompt indefinitely. A daily token ceiling bounds the worst day. An alert fires before that ceiling is reached, not when it's hit.


Each rule targets one of the leaks named earlier: unmetered output, unbounded retries, and no cap. None of them depends on a model's per-token price being low. They depend on someone having decided, per step, what the step is allowed to cost.


### Routing each step to the cheaper model


In Activepieces, a Router step sends a run down one of several branches depending on a condition you set, and each branch can call a different model.


The free plan's 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows are enough to test the routing before it carries real tickets.


Look at the canvas below for the shape: a Router at step 5 with two conditional branches and an Otherwise branch. The first two branches lead to separate agent steps for invoice payment work (steps 6 and 7).


Read it as a pricing decision. The condition on each branch is where you decide which tickets or emails are simple enough for a small model and which need a larger one.


The Otherwise branch matters most: it catches everything your conditions didn't anticipate. Point it at the cheap path, or at a human, rather than letting unclassified input default to the expensive model.


Set the retry cap at the step too, on the steps that call a model, so a malformed response costs two attempts at most.


### Provider-Side Spend Caps for Qwen3.8 Flash Next API


Don't rely on the workflow tool alone, and don't let it be the last line of defence. Most model providers let you set a monthly spend limit and a budget alert on the account or project that holds your API key. Set both.


The alert should sit below the limit, so you hear about a runaway step while there's still budget left.


Use a separate key for each workflow, with its own limit. A looping flow then exhausts its own allowance and stops, instead of draining the budget shared with everything else.


This works with any tool, and it still holds if a routing condition is written wrong.
